Hi Naomi,

Thanks for sending the draft order form yesterday — appreciate the fast turnaround. Our legal ops team reviewed the MSA skeleton and flagged two items we need to clarify before procurement signs:

1) Emergency relief: the MSA currently allows Redwood to seek injunctive relief in CA courts. Our counsel asked whether HighGroove can preserve the right to seek interim remedies in the customer’s home jurisdiction (we're UK-headquartered).
2) Forum for disputes: the draft relies on arbitration but is silent on where emergency court proceedings would be brought. We need to make sure the language doesn't preclude local preservation steps.

Can you confirm Redwood's standard approach to:
- specifying a governing law (you list Delaware in your template — is that negotiable?),
- allowing courts to grant urgent relief locally without waiving arbitration, and
- any operational requirements (e.g., boxed data access or logs for injunctive preservation)?

I've attached our annotated MSA redlines for reference. If it's easier, we can jump on a 20-min call with your GC and someone from legal ops to close this out.

Thanks,
Amanda Li
Contracts Lead | HighGroove

Amanda — thanks, got the redline. Looping Kim (legal) for the legal framing and Marcus for operational constraints. High-level:

- Governing law: our preference is Delaware for US-facing contracts, but we can accept customer-selected governing law for international customers provided we keep carveouts for injunctive relief.
- Emergency relief and arbitration: we typically allow courts to grant interim/preservation relief locally so long as the MSA explicitly states that seeking interim relief in court does not waive the requirement to arbitrate the underlying dispute.
- Operational asks: Marcus, can you confirm what we would need to support a preservation request (logs, snapshots, support SLAs) and any expected lead times?

Kim — can you draft a short clause we can propose to HighGroove that: (1) preserves local court access for emergency relief; (2) confirms arbitration as the exclusive remedy for merits; and (3) includes a narrow self-help / preservation procedure?

If helpful, we can propose a one-paragraph interim-relief checklist to append to the order form.

Naomi / Amanda — thanks for the context and the draft redline. Below are my proposed positions and a short clause you can drop into the MSA. I tried to balance HighGroove's need for local preservation with Redwood's preference for a single forum on the merits.

Position summary (recommended):
- Governing law: Accept customer-chosen governing law for the Order Form (we'll keep Delaware for the Master Services Agreement where feasible).
- Emergency relief: Carve out immediate injunctive/urgent relief to be available in any court of competent jurisdiction (including in the customer's local jurisdiction) solely for the purpose of preservation or to prevent irreparable harm; such relief is without prejudice to the parties' obligation to submit the underlying dispute to arbitration.
- Arbitration: Keep arbitration as exclusive forum for the merits, with mediation as a pre-condition (30 days) where feasible.
- Self-help: Narrow self-help language to allow Redwood to suspend service for breach related to security or payment after notice and short cure window — avoid broad unilateral termination rights.

Draft clause to propose: (drop-in)
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, either party may seek and obtain from any court of competent jurisdiction interim, provisional or injunctive relief necessary to preserve the status quo or prevent irreparable harm, including in the jurisdiction where the Customer is organized or where threatened harm may occur; such relief shall be without prejudice to the parties' obligation to submit the merits of the dispute to arbitration as set forth below."

Operational checklist (what we will provide on preservation requests):
- 24–48 hour turnaround for production of indexed logs relevant to the incident (subject to data retention policies).
- Snapshot exports of customer-specific KV-cache and model inference logs (if available) — requires approval from infra and may incur fees.
- Point-of-contact for legal and engineering during emergency requests (we should list these contacts in the Order Form appendix).

Marcus — can you confirm realistic turnaround for the two items above and any gating items (data residency, export tooling)? If there are platform-side blockers for a cross-border snapshot, flag them here.

Amanda — if this looks acceptable I can circulate a redline with the clause and the one-page preservation checklist attached.

—Kim

Kim / Naomi / Amanda — quick note from infra ops on what's feasible today and what requires a product change: 

- Logs: we can produce indexed inference logs and request traces within 24–48 hours for customers in our US and EU regions. For UK entities on EU region this is straightforward; for customers in APAC it may be longer (48–72 hours). Exports will be CSV/JSON and redaction of PII will occur per policy.
- Snapshots: a full KV-cache + transient runtime state snapshot is possible but not automated; it requires an ops playbook and a gated access request (privileged access), estimate 3–5 business days and a runbook sign-off. Cross-border export may require legal review (data residency).
- POC: happy to be named as technical POC in the appendix; we should also add a legal POC at Redwood for subpoena/service issues.

Operational ask to HighGroove: if you plan to seek local court preservation, please provide jurisdiction and the expected scope (logs only vs system snapshot) in the preservation notice so we can triage. We'll include a short form in the preservation checklist for that.

I'll support the redline with a short ops appendix describing timelines.

Thanks,
